text:
Without price data, I can't tell you whether COP rose or fell today. However, the news flow offers competing pressures on the stock. Oil prices remain elevated (US crude at $89.62, Brent at $92), which typically supports an oil producer like ConocoPhillips. But Trump's recent statements that the Iran conflict is "going to be ending fairly soon" and that "Iran militarily is effectively over" have pushed crude prices lower—Brent dipped below $90 for the first time since August on Monday. Lower oil prices compress profit margins for producers.

The broader political backdrop adds uncertainty. A midterm election blue wave against Trump and the GOP could shift energy policy away from oil and toward renewables, a structural headwind for traditional oil companies over time. That said, this shift plays out over months and years, whereas the immediate price pressure from de-escalation hopes in Iran is the more concrete near-term driver.
